Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the patient's vehicle was struck while the patient was turning left.
The patient reported low back pain and stiffness beginning shortly after the impact. The mechanism of injury described is
consistent with the lumbar strain diagnosed. Over the course of nine visits, care consisted of manual therapy, supervised
therapeutic exercise, and home exercise instruction. Treatment contiuned somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this type,
reflecting a slower-than-expected recovery of range of motion. Examination documented paraspinal muscle tenderness and
reduced lumbar flexion, findings that support the reported injury. Other testing, including neurological screening and straight leg
raise, was within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury to the lower back. Billing recodrs reflect single charges for
each service rendered, with no reepated or duplicate entries. Current assessment is lumbar strain, improving, with an anticipated
return to baseline function and discharge from active care once strength and mobility goals are met.
